content.value:
PR #10129 is CONFLICTING/DIRTY at head 514ff5c6f with all four required contexts GREEN — the block is purely the merge state, and its fence is clear (git merge-tree says SIX conflicting files and router.ex AUTO-MERGES; its three hunks at 1891/8755/8828 sit ~430 lines from wave 42's only router.ex claim at line 1460).

THE REAL BRAKE IS NOT THE FENCE. #9887 merged at 06:13:52Z carrying the ELEVEN-rung ladder, so origin/main's attentionRankOrder now reads removal_failed 1 / failed 2 / suspended 3 / degraded 4 / strained 5 / filling 6 / unreported 7 / behind 8 / removing 9 / provisioning 10 / ok 11, while #10129 asserts a TEN-rung ladder placing deploys_failing at 5 and unmetered at 9. A textual rebase mints a THIRTEEN-rung ladder and re-places both against three rungs that did not exist when wave 10 decided. semrole.go carries the same collision as load-bearing prose: main already reasons that strained(5)/filling(6)/unreported(7) sit between degraded(4) and behind(8), while #10129's added comment asserts deploys_failing sits at 5 between degraded(4) and behind(6). Both cannot be true.

Two fixtures PIN the ladder (attention_order.json and attention_order_cases.json), so resolving the .go files without regenerating both yields a green-looking tree whose fixture asserts a ladder the code no longer implements.

ALSO: #10129 and #10086 do NOT genuinely collide (10129 inserts at client.go:154, exactly #9887's anchor; #10086's seven hunks are all elsewhere) — order is free, and #10086 first is cheaper. The ONE genuine collision is #6028 (stale since 2026-07-31) on router.ex AND app.js, and app.js is wave 42's fence — clearing it to unblock #10129 breaches that fence by the back door.

This is a charter decision, not a merge resolution a builder may improvise. Charter D167.
